description: Heritage `value of … for key` on a NON-DICT container raises the byte-identical Core `ol-type` (issue #670, slice H5): the same `code`, `params` (`operation: "index"`, `expected: "list or dict"` — the Core selector's spelling, NOT a Heritage `"value of"`), `message`, `stage`, and `severity` a Core `:n["tom"]` selector raises when `:n` is a number (`spec/data-structures.md:183-195`). Proves the reader shares the Core dict-read's type check rather than inventing its own (`spec/conformance.md:146`: alternate spellings only, no new semantics), with NO Heritage spelling in any payload. The span points at the reader's `:n` operand sub-expression, the analog of the selector's `:n["tom"]` span (localization-only difference — `spec/localization.md`). Heritage depends on Data (`spec/conformance.md:301`), so both `data` and `heritage` are active.

diagnostics.message: index needs a list or dict, but got a number.
